cards.title: Google DeepMind Launches Gemini 4 Carbon: Frontier Reasoning for Cybersecurity and Long-Horizon Agents
cards.why_it_matters: Carbon is DeepMind's most capable model to date and ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, WANDR, and AutomationBench — a flagship release the whole field will be discussing.
cards.summary: Gemini 4 Carbon targets complex multi-step coding, scientific reasoning, and cybersecurity. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0, Perplexity WANDR, and Zapier AutomationBench at 2×+ lower cost per task than the next best external model, and #2 on the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark at 6×+ lower cost than the top performer. Priced at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, same as Gemini 4 Argon. A /swarm multi-agent preview launches in Google Antigravity.

cards.title: AlphaProof Code Formally Verifies Signal Protocol's Cryptographic Implementation in Four Weeks
cards.why_it_matters: First AI-assisted formal verification of a widely deployed cryptographic protocol at implementation depth — a landmark result for AI-driven software security and formal methods.
cards.summary: Google DeepMind's AlphaProof Code, a multi-LLM agentic framework, formally verified key security properties of Signal's actual compiled code using Lean theorem proving. Agents powered by Gemini Carbon generated over six million lines of Lean proofs; human experts reviewed only ~1% flagged by the system. The process took four weeks versus historically years. The system also correctly identified two reintroduced real bugs as insecure.

cards.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5 VLA Achieves 96% Success Rate on Mercedes-Benz Production Lines
cards.why_it_matters: Concrete real-world deployment data at industrial scale for a VLA model, with quantified success rates and speed improvements across 200+ tasks — a meaningful benchmark for physical AI.
cards.summary: Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2.5 vision-language-action model was evaluated across 200+ distinct tasks, achieving 30–100% higher success rates and 20–30% faster task completion versus prior baselines depending on task type. In a proof-of-concept with Apptronik's Apollo 2 humanoid on Mercedes-Benz automotive production lines, the system achieved a 96% success rate on automotive kitting. The model supports diverse robot morphologies and introduces adversarial jailbreak safety benchmarking for robotics.

cards.title: Decision Models: Structured Probability-Output Architectures Added to Hugging Face Transformers
cards.why_it_matters: Introduces a distinct inference paradigm — direct probability assignment over predefined options rather than autoregressive generation — with a new pipeline type in transformers, relevant for classification and routing use cases.
cards.summary: Decision models take a state and a set of predefined answer choices and return a probability distribution over those choices without generating text token-by-token. Hugging Face has added a 'decision' pipeline to transformers, with autotrust/GEV-26B-Decide as a reference model. The approach avoids JSON schema violations and constrained-decoding overhead common with LLM-based structured output, trading generation flexibility for reliability and speed on fixed-answer tasks.

cards.title: BotPsy: 0.8B On-Device Agent Beats Models 2.5× Its Size on Tool-Use Benchmarks
cards.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that sub-billion-parameter models can reach competitive agentic performance, directly relevant if you're building or evaluating on-device or privacy-preserving AI pipelines.
cards.summary: Tether AI's BotPsy (0.8B, built on Qwen3.5-0.8B) achieves SOTA tool-use across six benchmarks in the ≤1.2B class. It roughly doubles its base model's scores (BFCL v4: 23.4→44.0, ACEBench: 30.1→58.7, τ-bench: 23.2→51.5) and outperforms Qwen3.5-2B-Think on five of six benchmarks despite being 2.5× smaller. GGUFs available.

cards.title: Foundation Models vs. Task-Specific U-Nets for Medical Image Segmentation: DINOv2 Wins Out-of-Distribution
cards.why_it_matters: Provides concrete cross-institution generalization evidence for DINOv2-based adaptation — directly useful if you work on medical imaging or domain-shift robustness in segmentation.
cards.summary: DINOv2 fine-tuned with strategies from bias-only tuning to full fine-tuning was compared against U-Net and ResU-Net baselines on colonoscopy, breast ultrasound, and dermoscopy. The foundation model generalized better on every external dataset; task-specific models remained competitive within-distribution when training data were abundant and produced sharper boundaries but missed small lesions more often. Only a small fraction of DINOv2 required adaptation, with capacity needs driven by imaging domain rather than adaptation method.

cards.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Generated Adaptive Hints Improve RLVR Training Across Four Domains
cards.why_it_matters: Addresses a core inefficiency in RLVR — that outcome rewards discard rich trajectory information — with a teacher-driven scaffold approach that generalizes across ALFWorld, QA, math, and GPU kernel generation.
cards.summary: AutoScaffold uses a frozen teacher LLM to periodically diagnose student failures during RLVR training and generate task-class-level strategies and instance-level hints as prompt scaffolds, removed at evaluation. Gains over RL baselines without scaffolds: +7.2 points on ALFWorld success rate, +4.0 points average QA exact match, +5.0 points on GPU kernel tasks beating PyTorch reference. On math, the student surpasses QuestA's accuracy using ~one-third the training steps.

cards.title: Contrastive Discovery: Replacing Pointwise Hypothesis Testing with Contrast Sets for Scientific AI Agents
cards.why_it_matters: Offers a principled fix to a systematic flaw in LLM-based discovery agents — pointwise rejection without alternative identification — with strong empirical results across six domains.
cards.summary: Contrastive Discovery replaces single hypothesis testing with contrast sets: mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations scored by belief redistribution. On collected evidence, contrast sets resolve 73% of candidates that pointwise testing rejects without identifying an alternative. When guiding new experiments, contrast sets resolve 67% more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same budget. Human experts agreed with the resolved explanation on 78% of questions in a blinded study of 38 experts.

cards.title: Pyrite: LLM Agents Outperform Expert Chemists at Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking
cards.why_it_matters: Establishes a concrete benchmark where LLM-guided feature discovery outperforms both expert humans and direct LLM reasoning on a core drug discovery task, with GRPO enabling open-weight models to match frontier closed models.
cards.summary: Pyrite is a 1,500-pair pairwise pose-ranking benchmark across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists with 3D visualization and physics scores perform near chance. PyriteReasoner (direct LLM comparison) achieves 67% accuracy; PyriteFeaturizer (LLM-generated features for logistic regression) achieves 74%. GRPO fine-tuning of open-weight models enables them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models on this benchmark.

cards.title: TorchCurves: PyTorch Library for Differentiable B-Spline and Legendre Parametric Curves
cards.why_it_matters: Directly usable for KAN research, continuous embeddings, and functional regression — a practical building block for researchers exploring non-standard network architectures.
cards.summary: TorchCurves provides learnable parametric curves (B-spline and Legendre polynomial bases) as differentiable PyTorch modules. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with a surrounding model or produced by a network. The library supports KAN training, continuous feature embeddings, and functional regression. Timing experiments benchmark curve evaluation against NumPy/SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN, showing where overhead is substantial.
